hook_text: Imagine a soccer match with no rules, or a road with no traffic laws. What would happen?
clip_script: A classroom in Rustenburg. The learners write their own class rules: listen when others speak, keep the classroom clean, no bullying. Then a traffic officer visits. Speed limits, seatbelts and traffic lights are laws, made by government and enforced by officers and courts. Rules keep a group running smoothly. Laws keep a whole country safe and fair. But laws must be fair too, and under apartheid, many were not.
visual_style: Whiteboard classroom chart of rules, then a busy intersection with traffic lights, then a balance scale weighing fair and unfair laws.
mood: Friendly and practical, ending on a serious note about fairness.
pacing: Quick everyday examples, then a clear comparison of rules and laws, then a slower look at fairness.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write three fair rules for your classroom, with a reason for each.
